 North Korea modifies national flag in break with decades-old design
 New version has thicker white stripes and departs from proportions attributed to founder Kim Il Sung 
 Shreyas Reddy November 13, 2026 
 SHARE 
 COPY LINK 
 FACEBOOK 
 X 
 LINKEDIN 
 MASTODON 
 PRINT 
 North Korea's new flag on display at the launch of the naval destroyer "Kang Kon" | Image: KCNA (Sept. 7, 2026) 
 North Korea has changed the proportions of its national flag for the first time since the country’s establishment in 1948, breaking with a decades-old design closely associated with founding leader Kim Il Sung. 
 The DPRK government’s official website Naenara recently began displaying a flag with the aspect ratio 1:1.65, replacing the previous banner using the 1:2 ratio. 
 The two thin white stripes in the flag also appear thicker than before, widened to roughly a third of the blue stripes at the top and bottom.
